answer: The walnut of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Each submission hangs on the forge of a task receipt, and the island is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a cause and effect, two sentences register, it stays short. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, slashed on a failed audit, each submission carries a fresh nonce. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
